methodologyNotes: Covers handheld, self-powered LED flashlights sold at a published US MSRP, including EDC, tactical, and thrower models. Excludes headlamps, weapon-mounted lights, lanterns, and work lights. Price is typical US MSRP in USD. Performance figures use the manufacturer's ANSI/PLATO FL1 published ratings. maxLumens is peak (turbo) output in lumens. lowestLumens is the lowest/moonlight mode output in lumens. peakBeamIntensityCandela is peak beam intensity in candela (FL1). maxBeamDistanceMeters is rated throw in meters (FL1). maxRuntimeHrs is the longest rated runtime on the lowest useful mode, in hours. ledEmitter is the LED emitter model as named on the spec sheet (string). batteryType is the primary cell format (enum string, e.g. '21700 Li-ion', '14500/AA', 'built-in Li-ion'). rechargePort is the onboard charging interface (enum string: 'USB-C', 'magnetic', 'none'). ipRating is the ingress-protection rating (enum string, e.g. 'IP68', 'IPX8'). impactResistanceMeters is the rated drop/impact resistance in meters (FL1). lengthMm is overall length in millimeters. weightGrams is weight with the primary battery installed, in grams. Any value not disclosed by the manufacturer is null.

products.name: Olight Baton 4 Pro
products.priceNote: US MSRP $69.99, stated verbatim on the official Olight store product page ("Baton 4 Pro EDC Flashlight - 1600 Lumens USB-C", listed price $69.99) and corroborated at authorized Olight distributor BrightGuy ($69.99).
products.provenance: The official Olight store page confirms this exact model — "Baton 4 Pro EDC Flashlight - 1600 Lumens USB-C" at $69.99 — rated 1,600 lumens with a 200 m throw, 111 mm length, 114 g weight, powered by a 3,500 mAh 18650 battery with both MCC magnetic and USB-C charging; this distinguishes it from the sibling Baton Ultra (1,800 lm) and the non-Pro Baton 4 (1,300 lm). BrightGuy, an authorized Olight distributor, corroborates the same $69.99 price and provides the FL1 spec table: Olight 18650 Li-ion cell, IPX8 waterproof rating, and a 155-hour maximum runtime on the 15-lumen Low mode. Peak candela, LED emitter model, impact resistance, and the sub-1-lumen moonlight output were not stated verbatim on either fetched page, so those spec keys are left null.

products.name: Fenix PD36R Pro
products.priceNote: US MSRP $119.95, listed as "Regular price $119.95" on the official Fenix Store (fenix-store.com) product page, SKU FX-PD36R-PRO. The manufacturer page (fenixlight.com) does not publish a price.
products.provenance: The official Fenix manufacturer page (fenixlight.com/product/pd36r-pro) confirms this is the exact "PD36R PRO" model and states 2800 lumens max output, 380 m max beam distance, 42 h runtime, Luminus SFT70 LED, an included 5000 mAh 21700 Li-ion battery charged via USB-C, IP68 rating, and dimensions of 145.8 x 25.7 x 26.5 mm at 169 g including battery. The official US Fenix Store retailer page (fenix-store.com) corroborates the same model and figures, adds the Eco/lowest mode of 30 lumens and impact resistance of 1.5 meters, and provides the US price of $119.95 (SKU FX-PD36R-PRO). Peak beam intensity in candela is disclosed on neither page, so it is left null rather than computed from the beam distance.

products.name: Nitecore EDC29
products.priceNote: US price $109.95 as listed on the official Nitecore Store retailer page (nitecorestore.com, "$109.95"); the same $109.95 also appears at The Home Depot. The manufacturer product page publishes no price.
products.provenance: The official Nitecore product page (nitecore.com/product/edc29) confirms this exact model — the EDC29 "Ultra Slim High Performance EDC Flashlight" — and its FULL SPEC lists 6,500 lm max output, 40,230cd peak intensity, 400 m throw, 61 h max runtime, 2 x NiteLab UHi 20 MAX LEDs, a built-in 2,500 mAh Li-ion battery with USB-C charging, IP54, 1 m impact resistance, 133.5 mm length and 160 g weight. The Nitecore Store retailer page (SKU FL-NITE-EDC29) corroborates the same EDC29 model, its 15-lumen Ultralow lowest mode, IP54 rating and 1 m impact resistance, and lists the US price at $109.95. Candela/throw follow the manufacturer's FL1 figures (the retailer's 35,360 cd conflicts and was not used); price is taken from the retailer since the manufacturer page publishes none, and no release date is stated on either page.

products.name: Streamlight Wedge
products.priceNote: US MSRP is not published on the Streamlight manufacturer page. priceUsd = 101.86 sourced verbatim from BrightGuy, an authorized Streamlight dealer, which lists the Wedge "From $101.86" (price range "$101.86 – $106.62" across colors; the 88810 black is the base/starting price). This is the current dealer street price, not a list MSRP.
products.provenance: The Streamlight manufacturer page confirms this is the exact Wedge EDC flashlight and its FL1 spec table gives Lumens (High) 1,000, Run Time (Low) 3.00 hours, Beam Distance (High) 110 meters, Candela (High) 3,000, Length 5.46 in (13.87 cm), Weight 93.55 grams, plus "IPX7 waterproof to 1m; 1m impact resistance tested" and USB-C charging; the 300-lumen constant-on / 1,000-lumen THRO burst modes are described in the body text. The BrightGuy authorized-dealer page corroborates the same model (part number 88810), matching 1000/300 lumens, 110 m beam, IPX7, USB-C, and a built-in Lithium Polymer rechargeable cell, and supplies the price "From $101.86" (range $101.86–$106.62). peakBeamIntensityCandela uses the manufacturer's peak (THRO) value of 3,000 cd (2·√3000 ≈ 110 m confirms it is the peak). No LED emitter model and no release year are stated on either fetched page, so both are null; lengthMm 138.7 is the exact conversion of the manufacturer's stated 13.87 cm (length is published only in inches/cm).

products.name: ThruNite T1S
products.priceNote: US price $39.95 for the black (Cool White) T1S at publication time, per ZeroAir review (dated 2021-12-24): "The Thrunite T1S flashlight ships for a reasonable $39.95" and "Price in USD at publication time: $39.95 (black)". The grey body is listed at $45.95.
products.provenance: Two independent dated reviews reproducing ThruNite's official T1S spec sheet were fetched, since ThruNite's own store page is JS-rendered and the official T1S.pdf is image-only with no extractable text. ZeroAir (dated 2021-12-24) confirms the exact original T1S model — Luminus SST-40 emitter, 1212 claimed lumens, 184 m claimed throw, 1×18350 cell, USB-C charging, and 69.5×26.5×22 mm dimensions — and states the US price as $39.95 for the black/Cool White version at publication time. 1Lumen corroborates the Luminus SST-40 emitter, 1,212 lumens, 18350 cell, USB-C charging, IPX8 rating, 69.5 mm length, and 71 g weight-with-cell, and explicitly distinguishes this original T1S from the later 1080-lumen "T1S v2", confirming model identity.

products.name: Wurkkos TS10
products.priceNote: US price $19.99 per the dated ZeroAir review (2022-10-25): "This light is available right now for the incredible price of $19.99!" and its table row "Price in USD at publication time: $19.99." This is the typical US MSRP for the original TS10.
products.provenance: The Wurkkos manufacturer product listing confirms the original TS10 configuration — three 90-CRI CSP LEDs plus single-color aux LEDs (distinguishing it from the later V2's RGB aux, the single-LED TS10 SG, and the 18650 TS10 MAX), a single 14500 Li-Ion cell, 71.5 mm length and the Anduril 2 UI. The dated ZeroAir review (2022-10-25) independently confirms this exact original model and its manufacturer FL1 claims: 1400 lumens, 129 m claimed throw, "CSP LED" emitter, no onboard charging, and 71.5 mm length. ZeroAir also states the US price verbatim — "the incredible price of $19.99" and "Price in USD at publication time: $19.99" — the figure recorded here.

products.name: Wuben X3 Owl
products.priceNote: Manufacturer store wubenlight.com lists 'White X3 + Base (Black)' and 'Black X3 + Base (Black)' at $39.99 (the flashlight with its charging base) verbatim; the aluminum charging-box bundle is $87.99 and the charging base accessory alone is $16.99. Used $39.99 as the US MSRP for the flashlight itself.
products.provenance: The Wuben official store page (wubenlight.com) confirmed the exact model 'WUBEN Lightok X3 Owl Compact Rechargeable EDC Flashlight' and listed the standard X3 + charging Base configuration at $39.99, plus 'max 700 lumens' output and 'Weighing just 65g' verbatim. The 1Lumen hands-on review corroborates the same X3 Owl and supplies the manufacturer-specified FL1 figures: Samsung LH351D white + Luminus SST10 red emitters, 700 lm max output, 102 m beam distance, 2,590 cd specified turbo peak intensity, 50 h specified Low-mode runtime, IP65 rating, proprietary magnetic + wireless onboard charging (no USB port on the light), a built-in 1,000 mAh cell, and a 70 mm measured length. Both pages describe the single X3 Owl model (not a different capacity or variant), so the model-identity check passes; lowestLumens and impactResistanceMeters were not stated on either fetched page and are left null.

products.name: Acebeam E10 2.0
products.priceNote: Acebeam official store product page lists the E10 2.0 at $59.90. Notebookcheck's dated launch article corroborates a debut price of "$60".
products.provenance: The official Acebeam product page (source) confirms this is the exact E10 2.0 model and provides the full ANSI/PLATO FL1 spec table verbatim: CREE XP-LR LED, 1200 lm turbo, 2 lm UltraLow (120h), 127806 cd / 715 m throw, IP68, 1.5 m impact, 88 mm length, 106.5 g with the included 16340 USB-C rechargeable Li-ion battery, and a listed price of $59.90. Notebookcheck's dated launch article (corroboration, published 12/21/2025) independently confirms the same model, its $60 debut price, the 1,200 lm / 782 yd (715 m) throw, 2 lm/120 h low mode, IP68, magnetic tail, and 16340 cell. Notebookcheck also states the charging electronics (USB-C) sit on the removable battery and are "not part of the flashlight," so the flashlight body itself has no onboard charging port (rechargePort = "none").

products.name: Sofirn IF22A
products.priceNote: No US MSRP or retail price could be sourced from a fetchable page. The official Sofirn store (sofirnlight.com) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, and the 1Lumen review shows only a "See price at Sofirn" link with no figure. priceUsd left null rather than guessing.
products.provenance: The official Sofirn product page is the canonical listing for this exact model (the TIR-optic IF22A, distinct from the reflector-based IF22 sibling), but it returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching, so its figures could not be machine-verified. The 1Lumen hands-on review (corroboration) confirmed the exact model identity and carried the manufacturer spec sheet verbatim: 2,100 lumens turbo, 1-lumen moonlight, 121,333 cd beam intensity (manufacturer "Specs" column), IPX8, single 21700 cell, Luminus SFT40 emitter, and onboard USB-C charging, plus review-measured overall length 127.1 mm and weight-with-cell 193 g. Rated throw in meters (Sofirn markets 680 m yet its own 121,333 cd spec implies ~697 m), rated low-mode runtime, impact resistance, and US price were not verbatim on the fetchable corroboration page, so those are null.

products.name: Olight Arkfeld Pro
products.priceNote: US MSRP $89.99 as listed verbatim on the Olight official store page ("$89.99", Arkfeld Pro Flat EDC Flashlight, Black CW). BrightGuy independently lists the same original price ("$89.99", current sale $82.99). MSRP taken as $89.99.
